strings.name: Kai-Fu Lee
strings.role: AI researcher; 01.AI founder and CEO; Sinovation Ventures chairman
strings.summary: Kai-Fu Lee moved from speech-recognition research into technology management at Apple, SGI, Microsoft and Google, helping establish Microsoft Research China. He founded Sinovation Ventures in 2009 and 01.AI in 2023, linking investment, startups and enterprise AI. Books including AI Superpowers discuss work and industry; his forecasts are views rather than verified outcomes.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributes to speech-recognition research and technology-company management, founds Sinovation Ventures, and promotes AI entrepreneurship and public education.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Computer-science bachelor's, Columbia University; computer-science PhD, Carnegie Mellon University
strings.highlights.h1.title: Speech-recognition research
strings.highlights.h1.text: During his doctorate, supervised by Raj Reddy, he developed Sphinx with Roberto Bisiani and others, advancing large-vocabulary, speaker-independent continuous recognition.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Technology, investment and public debate
strings.highlights.h2.text: Through Sinovation, 01.AI and popular books, he supports technology startups and discusses AI's effects on work and corporate organization.
strings.timeline.t1.title: AI Native US hardcover published
strings.timeline.t1.text: The book examines how organizations and workflows can adapt to AI; ebook and audio editions had appeared earlier.
strings.timeline.t2.title: 01.AI shifts toward enterprise applications
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company stopped pretraining larger models from scratch and moved toward tailored enterprise AI using models such as DeepSeek.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founding 01.AI
strings.timeline.t3.text: He established 01.AI as CEO, initially developing Yi large language models and later enterprise applications.
strings.timeline.t4.title: AI Superpowers published
strings.timeline.t4.text: He examined Chinese and US AI industries, changing employment and social responses, expanding public debate.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Founding Sinovation Ventures
strings.timeline.t5.text: After leaving Google, he announced the Beijing investment and venture-building organization supporting technology entrepreneurs.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining Google to lead China operations
strings.timeline.t6.text: He moved from Microsoft and later served as Greater China president; a noncompete dispute led to litigation settled that December.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joining Microsoft Research
strings.timeline.t7.text: He moved from SGI and established and led Microsoft Research China that year; it was later renamed Microsoft Research Asia.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joining Apple
strings.timeline.t8.text: He moved from Carnegie Mellon into industry and successively led speech, multimedia and interactive-media teams.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Doctorate and Sphinx research
strings.timeline.t9.text: He earned his Carnegie Mellon computer-science PhD; Sphinx demonstrated continuous-recognition advances that year, and he stayed on to teach.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Columbia undergraduate degree
strings.timeline.t10.text: He completed computer science and went on to research at Carnegie Mellon.
